report_name: CISA & FBI Detail Escalating Medusa Ransomware Tactics

threat_actors.name: Medusa
threat_actors.description: A Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) group active since at least 2021 that has compromised over 500 organizations by April 2026. The group is known for rapidly weaponizing newly disclosed vulnerabilities, using initial access brokers, and employing a double-extortion model, primarily targeting the Healthcare and Public Health (HPH) sector.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware and data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Medusa gains initial access by exploiting vulnerabilities in public-facing applications, such as Fortinet EMS, Fortra GoAnywhere, and BeyondTrust products, often within 24 hours of their public disclosure.

attack_patterns.name: Valid Accounts
attack_patterns.description: The Medusa group leverages credentials purchased from initial access brokers to gain entry into victim networks.

attack_patterns.name: Disable or Modify Tools
attack_patterns.description: Medusa actors terminate processes and stop services associated with Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) and antivirus solutions using tools like `sc.exe` and `net.exe` to evade defenses.

attack_patterns.name: Windows Command Shell
attack_patterns.description: Medusa affiliates use `cmd.exe` for command execution as part of their living-off-the-land techniques to blend in with normal network activity.

attack_patterns.name: PowerShell
attack_patterns.description: The Medusa group uses PowerShell for scripting to maintain persistence and evade detection.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
attack_patterns.description: Medusa actors escalate privileges by exploiting local vulnerabilities or using stolen administrator credentials.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
attack_patterns.description: Before encryption, Medusa actors exfiltrate sensitive data to actor-controlled infrastructure, often using legitimate cloud storage services to make the traffic harder to detect.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The Medusa ransomware encrypts victim data as part of its double-extortion model.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Medusa actors delete volume shadow copies using `vssadmin.exe` to prevent system restoration from backups.

malware.name: Medusa Ransomware
malware.description: The primary payload of the Medusa group, often named `medusa.exe`. It is used to encrypt victim data and exfiltrate it for double-extortion purposes.

tools.name: sc.exe
tools.description: Used by Medusa actors to stop security-related services as a defense evasion technique.

tools.name: net.exe
tools.description: Used by Medusa actors to stop security-related services and for network enumeration.

tools.name: cmd.exe
tools.description: Used by Medusa affiliates for command execution as a living-off-the-land technique.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description: Used by Medusa affiliates for scripting as a living-off-the-land technique.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: Used by Medusa actors to delete volume shadow copies to inhibit system recovery.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2023-48788
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in Fortinet FortiClient EMS exploited by the Medusa ransomware group for initial access.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2025-10035
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in Fortra GoAnywhere MFT exploited by the Medusa ransomware group for initial access.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-1731
vulnerabilities.description: A vulnerability in BeyondTrust exploited by the Medusa ransomware group for initial access.

identities.name: University of Mississippi Medical Center
identities.description: A healthcare organization cited as a victim of a Medusa ransomware attack.

identities.name: Healthcare and Public Health sector
identities.description: A primary target sector for the Medusa ransomware group.

infrastructure.name: Medusa Exfiltration Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Actor-controlled infrastructure, including legitimate cloud storage services, used to exfiltrate victim data before encryption as part of the double-extortion scheme.

indicators.name: Medusa Ransomware Associated Files
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Medusa Ransomware Associated Files Created
id: 2b1f8c9a-7d6e-4f5a-8b3c-1d2e3f4a5b6c
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of files commonly associated with Medusa ransomware, including the main executable and the ransom note.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa25-071a
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-18
tags:
  - attack.t1486
level: critical
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\medusa.exe'
      - '\!!!READ_ME_MEDUSA!!!.txt'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the creation of the Medusa ransomware executable (`medusa.exe`) or its ransom note (`!!!READ_ME_MEDUSA!!!.txt`).

indicators.name: Medusa Volume Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: Medusa Volume Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 9e8d7c6b-5a4f-4e3d-8c2b-1a9f8e7d6c5b
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by Medusa ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa25-071a
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-18
tags:
  - attack.t1490
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
      - '/all'
      - '/quiet'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects attempts to delete volume shadow copies using `vssadmin.exe`, a technique used by Medusa to prevent system recovery.

indicators.name: Medusa Security Service Stoppage
indicators.pattern:
title: Medusa Security Service Stoppage
id: 1a2b3c4d-5e6f-4a7b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of sc.exe or net.exe to stop services, a technique used by Medusa actors to disable security tools.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa25-071a
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-18
tags:
  - attack.t1562.001
level: medium
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\sc.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'stop'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of `sc.exe` or `net.exe` to stop system services, a common defense evasion technique employed by Medusa to disable security software.
